checksums.name: slot_trailer_candidate
checksums.formula_detail: 4-byte trailer 65 B9 86 CA at relative offset 0x70 of each 116-byte active block (absolute 0x0270, 0x0370, 0x0470, 0x0570, 0x0670, 0x0770). Tested sum8/sum16/sum32, word-wise XOR32, CRC16-CCITT (poly 0x1021), CRC32 (zlib standard poly), one's- and two's-complement sum32 over payload ranges [0x00:0x70], [0x08:0x70], [0x0C:0x70], [0x00:0x6C], [0x00:0x68], [0x00:0x60], in both little-endian and big-endian trailer interpretations, and against each individual trailer byte. No algorithm/range combination reproduced the stored value. Could be a fixed hardcoded magic constant rather than a computed checksum.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change 00 00 00 00 to 01 00 00 00 in slot 0 only (offset 0x208), leaving other slots untouched
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If read by the game as a flag/counter, expect a visible change in slot-select UI, continue-state, or (if checksum-validated) the slot being flagged corrupt on load. No observed change would suggest the field is reserved/unused.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Zero out trailer 65 B9 86 CA to 00 00 00 00 in slot 0 only (offset 0x270), leaving payload bytes 0x200-0x26F unchanged
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If the field is a validated magic/checksum, expect slot 0 to be treated as corrupt/reset to default on load while untouched slots 1-5 remain normal. If no effect, the field is likely unvalidated or unread.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip individual bytes within the 0x99-filled body (offsets 0x200-0x207 and 0x20C-0x26F of slot 0) from 0x99 to 0x00, one at a time
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If any byte is rendered as a name/score/progress value in-game, expect a visible proportional change, allowing the 100-byte blob to be subdivided into real sub-fields.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Mutate only slot 2's trailer (offset 0x470) so it differs from the other five identical slots
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Tests the redundancy hypothesis: if slots are independent records, only slot 2's in-game state changes; if slots are redundant mirrors with majority-vote/first-valid-copy selection, the game may silently repair slot 2 or ignore the difference.

open_questions: No save-related function (writer, reader, serializer, checksum, or hardware I/O driver) could be identified: ghidra/save_related_functions.c reports 0 MMIO seeds across all 98 traced functions, meaning the capture never executed any save I/O code path for this title. A re-trace capturing an actual in-game save action is required before any function-level claim can be made.

The 4-byte trailer 65 B9 86 CA at the end of each 116-byte active block does not match sum8/16/32, word-XOR32, CRC16-CCITT, or CRC32 over any tested payload range/endianness combination. It may be a fixed magic constant rather than a computed checksum; cannot be resolved without a second .sav sample where the payload differs.

Whether the six 256-byte-stride slots are six independent save records or six redundant mirrors of one logical record cannot be determined: all six are byte-identical in the only available sample, and no selection/voting code was traced.

The 4-byte zero field at relative offset 0x08 of each slot (absolute 0x208, 0x308, ...) could be a counter, flag, or reserved padding; indistinguishable with a single static sample showing it at its initial value in every slot.
The 512-byte region 0x0000-0x01FF is entirely blank (0xFF) in this sample; unknown whether it is unused or an unwritten global-config/header area.
No paired .ss save states are present in this packet (states/ is empty), so none of the fuzzing_targets mutations have yet been tested against live emulator reload behavior.
